Recently, general humanoid robot company LimX Dynamics announced the completion of a nearly $200 million Pre-IPO funding round, with a post-investment valuation of 15 billion yuan, entering the ranks of super hundred-billion unicorns. The company has accumulated $400 million in total funding over the past six months, solidifying its foundation for future capital market operations.

The funding round gathered leading global capital from China, Europe, the Middle East, North America, and Southeast Asia, reflecting global market recognition of the long-term value of embodied intelligence and confidence in LimX Dynamics' technology roadmap, product capabilities, and globalization strategy. New investors include IDG Capital, Lens Technology, pan-European industrial investment group G.G.G.Group and Redstone VC, Huashan Capital, and Hefei Binhu Industrial Development Group. UAE-based Stone Venture participated in multiple consecutive rounds, while existing investors such as Oasis Capital, Cornerstone Capital, Nanshan Zhanxin, Shangqi Capital, and NIO Capital made additional oversubscriptions.

Founded in 2022 with its global headquarters in Shenzhen, LimX Dynamics is an AI-driven general humanoid robot company focused on full-size humanoid robot development, while also launching innovative products such as the multi-form robot TRON. Centered on three core areas—hardware design and manufacturing, brain-body fusion technology, and the embodied intelligent agent OS system—the company unleashes AGI's generalization capabilities in the physical world, advancing embodied intelligence in research, commercial, and home applications.

La compañía ha completado una financiación acumulada de 400 millones de dólares en los últimos seis meses, consolidando la base para futuras operaciones en los mercados de capitales. Según se informa, esta ronda de financiación reunió a los principales capitales globales de China, Europa, Oriente Medio, América del Norte y el Sudeste Asiático, reflejando plenamente el reconocimiento del mercado global del valor a largo plazo de la industria de la inteligencia integrada, así como la confianza en la ruta tecnológica, la capacidad de producto y la estrategia de globalización de LimX Dynamics. On July 13, Stepfun held a launch event in Shanghai, officially releasing the world's first agent-native operating system Step AOS (Step Agentic-native OS), the personal agent Step Amoo built on the model matrix and Step AOS, and the large model-native AI terminal brand STEPX. The world's first large model-native agent smartphone STEPX Neo also debuted at the event. With this, Stepfun has established a "model-software-hardware" tripartite technical closed loop encompassing models, systems, and terminals. Leiphone.com  

Building a runtime environment for agents from scratch. After years of rapid development, AI has arrived at the threshold of the agent era. But for agents to truly enter people's daily lives, smart models alone are not enough. There are three walls ahead: the memory wall, the decision wall, and the action wall. Agents cannot remember users, struggle to autonomously make judgments for complex tasks, and are even less able to systematically complete various tasks on behalf of users. Stepfun believes this is a structural problem at the operating system level that cannot be solved by adding features within individual applications.  

Stepfun's solution is not the industry-common "OS+AI" approach, but rather, following the principle of human-machine symbiosis, building a runtime environment for agents from scratch—this is Step AOS. "Open a door for an agent on an old system, and it will always be a visitor. Build a house for an agent, and it becomes a native resident."  

Step AOS brings three layers of innovation: new infrastructure, new energy
